problem_statement: Paging through our records must visit every row exactly once, in (created_at, id) order, however many rows share a created_at. It does not: when a page boundary falls inside a group of rows with the same created_at, rows from that group go missing from the walk, and clients that key on id see gaps. A cursor must carry everything the resume needs — decoding one must give back exactly the pair it was built from — and a resume must start strictly after the row the cursor names, so that every page size walks the same complete sequence. A token that was not produced by encode_cursor, or a page size below 1, must be rejected with ValueError rather than accepted.
